claims.claim_ar: الواو في بداية الجملة تعمل استئنافاً/فصلاً يتوقف عنده السياق ويؤكد الانتقال إلى بيان عجز المعبودين؛ أي فصل/استدراك لبيان حكم جديد.
claims.claim_en: The conjunction waw functions as an introductory/interrupting 'waw' (istinaaf), producing a pause/transition that emphasizes the new statement (the impotence of the deities).
claims.needs_review_reason: Inference from grammatical label '(الواو) استئنافية' in the source; a classical rhetorical citation (Jurjani/Sakkaki etc.) would strengthen certainty.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Highlights and foregrounds the assertion of the idols' impotence, creating emphasis through discontinuity/arrival at a new, decisive statement.

claims.claim_ar: استعمال اسم الموصول «الذين» لتحديد جماعة معيّنة من الدعاة لغير الله — وظيفة تعريفية/تعيينية تضيف وضوحاً وتخصيصاً في الحكم البلاغي.
claims.claim_en: The relative pronoun 'al-ladhina' is used to specify/define a particular group (those you call upon besides Him), a definitional device that makes the judgement pointed and concrete.
claims.needs_review_reason: Based on grammatical tagging '(الذين) موصول مبتدأ' in the source; classification as tarif/tankir (definitional/contrastive function) is a rhetorical reading requiring corroboration from dedicated balagha sources.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Focuses attention on the specific agents being criticised, sharpening the negative judgement.

claims.claim_ar: تكرار أداة النفي «لا ... ولا» يكوّن أسلوباً تأكيدياً؛ التكرار البلاغي يقوّي نفي القدرة عن المعبودين ويزيد من التأكيد.
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the negation particle 'la' ('la ... wa la') forms an emphatic rhetorical structure; the repetition strengthens the negation of the deities' power.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source explicitly labels '(لا) حرف نفي'; the rhetorical effect (repetition for emphasis) is a standard balagha reading but could be supported by a balagha-specific citation.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Intensifies the denial of help/ability, producing stronger rhetorical repudiation.

claims.claim_ar: التوازي بين «لا يستطيعون نصركم» و«ولا أنفسهم ينصرون» يمثل مقابلة/موازنة تبرز المعنى عبر تكرار الفكرة بصيغتين متوازيتين؛ واو العطف تؤمّن الربط والتوازي.
claims.claim_en: The parallelism between 'they cannot help you' and 'nor can they help themselves' constitutes a muqabalah (balanced parallelism); the coordinating waw supports the balance, reinforcing the point by repeating the idea in matched clauses.
claims.needs_review_reason: Inference from grammatical coordination '(الواو) عاطفة' to the rhetorical device of muqabalah; a direct classical balagha reference would make this identification firmer.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Creates rhetorical balance that doubles the force of the negation and underlines the helplessness of the invoked beings.
